question: Does response-outcome recoverability support a distinct empirical methods paper, by changing source-grounded trial interpretations after resolving denominator, arm identity, measurement unit, unevaluable patients, confirmation or duration?
estimand: In a bounded explicitly purposive pilot, distinguish extraction errors from genuine reporting ambiguity and assess whether correcting either changes an actual reported/prespecified study interpretation. No prevalence estimate from pilot.
rank: Next existing rank3 prospect after atlas and fusion-benchmark evidence-based deprioritization. Broad evidence-synthesis utility and independently accessible trial sources; weaker EMC specificity and unproven novelty. Cheap retrieval does not confer rank.
scope: Freeze deterministic pilot selection before retrieval: at most12 distinct trials, balancing unit/denominator/duplicate-arm risks and ordinary included records; if original negative-screen identifiers/raw caches accessible include extractor negatives. Original literature-cache refs absent in current clone: do not mistake unavailable cache for unavailable public record. Current primary registry retrieval must be timestamped and version differences distinguished.
success: At least two independently source-resolvable consequential interpretation discrepancies plus a defensible methodological contribution beyond fixing our extractor or counting missing fields; actual study-defined decision criteria required for trial success/failure claims. This is a development gate, not publication adequacy.
failure: Only own extraction bugs, missing-field counts, tautological DCR-minus-ORR arithmetic, invented decision thresholds, or unavailable adequate reference outcomes. Preserve defects but do not manufacture a paper.
stop: One fresh-context worker, own bounded goal,medium,1800seconds, no nested agents/tasks/runners. Inspect small primary sample and targeted novelty prior art; return go/no-go and exact next question. No manuscript edits or registry edits, no protocol rewrite, no full-corpus reanalysis.
